implementation_statement: The EHR vendor provides account management functions. The owner creates and removes accounts: the owner's own account and the billing company's named billing-role accounts. Gap: no periodic review of accounts, and the IT consultant's remote-support account on the laptop had unattended access (P07).
evidence: EHR user list; remote-support tool settings

implementation_statement: The EHR enforces role-based access. The owner assigns the provider/administrator role to the owner and the billing role to billing company users.
evidence: EHR role settings; vendor SOC 2 report (P09)

implementation_statement: Tablet and phone lock after 1 minute with a passcode. Gap: the laptop locked only after 15 minutes idle; the owner is resetting it to 5 minutes.
The owner has only CME exposure. The owner will complete an annual HIPAA security course and subscribe to monthly security reminders by 2026-11-30.
The EHR vendor logs sign-ins and record access for every user. The owner relies on this logging (SOC 2 report, P09).
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; EHR audit log screen

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: No one has ever reviewed the EHR audit log or the email sign-in history. Starting 2026-10, the owner will review both on the first clinic day of each month and log the review.
The BIA (P05), POL-01 contingency section, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: the coverage arrangement and sealed emergency access sheet are not in place yet (due 2026-12-31).

The EHR vendor backs up the medical record (inherited; RPO 1 hour stated in its SOC 2 system description). Owner responsibility: downloads, documents, and clinical photos on the laptop and phone have no backup.
Each person has a unique account in the EHR (owner and each billing company user). The owner does not share credentials.

The EHR vendor enforces MFA for every account, including the owner's practice-administrator account. Owner responsibility: protect the phone that holds the second factor and store recovery codes offline.

provider_if_inherited: EHR vendor; email and file provider; cloud fax vendor
implementation_statement: MFA is enforced for the EHR. Gap: MFA is available but not turned on for the consumer email account or the cloud fax portal. Owner turns both on by 2026-09-15.
The ransomware runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-08-31 with a contact list. Gap: contacts not yet printed and the plan has not been walked through (due 2026-09-30).
Paper is shredded through the building-provided locked shredding bin. Gap: no procedure for wiping or destroying old laptops, phones, and tablets.
The landlord controls the building entrances and reception. The owner locks the exam suite and the paper file cabinet when leaving.
First risk analysis completed 2026-07-24 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed each July and after major changes.

BAAs on file: EHR vendor, billing company, cloud fax vendor, and IT consultant (signed 2026-07-17). Gap: no BAA with the email and file provider or the answering service; the AI scribe app was used with none.
Denial-of-service protection for the EHR and portal is provided by the vendor and its hosting provider.
The laptop's built-in host firewall is on. Gap: the suite uses the shared building Wi-Fi (separate password, same network as other tenants). A practice-owned router is planned by 2026-12-31.
The EHR, portal, and cloud fax use TLS (inherited). Gap: the owner texts patients by ordinary SMS from a personal phone. Messages move to the EHR portal by 2026-10-31.

The EHR vendor encrypts data at rest (inherited). Tablet and phone are encrypted by their passcodes. Gap: the laptop has no full-disk encryption; the owner turns on the built-in encryption by 2026-09-15.
The EHR vendor patches the application. Automatic OS updates are on for the laptop, tablet, and phone; the owner restarts when prompted.
The operating system's built-in antivirus runs real-time scanning with automatic signature updates. Owner responsibility: keep it on and act on alerts.
